title: Westward, Lord, the World Alluring
description: Westward, Lord, the World Alluring in Tonic Solfa to LUX EOI, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Arthur Cleveland Coxe wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 418, “Western Missions”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7 D) (8.7.8.7.8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to LUX EOI; any other Eights and Sevens Double (8.7.8.7 D) tune fits them as well.
underlay: West-ward, Lord, the world al-lur-ing, Has Thy ri-sen day star beamed, And, the sink-ing soul as-sur-ing, O'er the world's wide o-cean streamed. West-ward, still, the mid-night break-ing, West-ward, still, its light be poured! Hea-then Thy pos-ses-sion mak-ing, Ut-most lands Thy dwell-ing, Lord!

lines: O'er the world's wide ocean streamed.
Westward, still, its light be poured!
Let thy starlight, Son of Mary,
Here be heard, ye herald voices,
Till the Lord his glory shows,
With the bloom of Sharon's rose.
And the trees of ages nod,
Make a highway for our God.
Westward, till the church be kneeling
In the forest aisles so dim,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Arthur Cleveland Coxe died in 1896.
credits: Words by Arthur Cleveland Coxe (1818–1896), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to LUX EOI by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
